confirmed: The source is the full arXiv:2507.03307v1 dated 4 Jul 2025; the title and author order match the form, and the PDF has 17 pages (PDF p. 1, version stamp and author block; PDF pp. 1-17).

The entire markdown was read through the final reference; the PDF ends with references and contains no appendix, and supplementary material is not stated (PDF pp. 14-17, conclusion and references; full document).

One within-person user study compares Reverger with its restricted AI baseline. Latin Square counterbalancing is stated, but random allocation to sequences is not; randomized counts appropriately remain null (PDF p. 6, Section 5; p. 7, Table 1 and Section 5.4).

There are 16 distinct participants recruited through Upwork, with P1-P16 represented in both tool conditions and in the interaction logs. The per-arm analyzed counts refer to the same people; the total analyzed count is 16, below 50, and exclusions are not stated (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 5.3 and Table 1; p. 9, Table 2; p. 14, Sections 7.3 and 8).

Both tools use generative AI; the baseline disables recursive exploration and simultaneous selection of multiple directions. The model is claude-3-sonnet-20240229 (PDF p. 5, Section 4.2; p. 6, Section 5.1).
Participants modified supplied summaries of Cinderella and Alice in Wonderland, with 10 minutes per task and extra time allowed on request (PDF p. 6, Section 5.2; p. 7, Section 5.4.2).

CSI and NASA-TLX are self-reports of creativity support and workload. Table 2 counts directions revealed and generation attempts, while interviews describe preferences; no creativity or diversity score on participant-produced output is reported (PDF p. 8, Sections 5.5-6.1; p. 9, Table 2; pp. 10-12, Sections 6.2.2-6.4).
S1-O1.reported matches the PDF: exploration, z = ?4.56, p = .038, from the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test. It is perceived support for exploration, not an output creativity score (PDF p. 8, Section 6.1).
S1-O2.reported matches the PDF: results worth effort, z = ?4.82, p = .003, from the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test. It is a self-report about the tool (PDF p. 8, Section 6.1).
The one-line finding accurately reproduces the analyzed sample count and both printed survey statistics and identifies their self-report basis (PDF p. 8, Section 6.1; p. 9, Table 2).

The other design classification, core exclusion, and context_class none are supported: randomization is not stated, the sample is below the threshold, and no qualifying output score is reported. There is no study meeting the requested randomized-people-plus-output-score definition (PDF pp. 6-10, Sections 5-6.2.2; p. 14, Section 7.3).
This is an original tool evaluation, not a synthesis; no pooled estimates or study-count extraction is applicable (PDF p. 6, Section 5; pp. 8-12, Section 6).
summary: The 16-person study has no stated randomization or qualifying output score, and the recorded survey statistics match the PDF. The form needs one correction: four authors list Midjourney affiliations, so company involvement should be true.
